classification.difficultyReason: Calculate two fractions of the total, then subtract both quantities to find the remainder.

content.prompt: There were 60 people at a party. If $\frac{1}{5}$ of the people wore red, $\frac{1}{4}$ wore blue and the rest wore white, how many people wore white?

answer.worked:
The whole is 60 people. For red, one part is $\frac{1}{5}$ of the whole; for blue, one part is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the whole.

$$\begin{align*}\text{People wearing red}&=60\div5\\\text{People wearing red}&=12\\\text{People wearing blue}&=60\div4\\\text{People wearing blue}&=15\\\text{People wearing white}&=60-12-15\\\text{People wearing white}&=33\end{align*}$$
